extracted.intended_audience: members of the American Mathematical Society; mathematicians planning to submit meeting abstracts, letters to the Notices, meeting announcements, classified ads, or to change membership/contact information
extracted.subtask_short: submitting abstracts and letters to AMS
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, deadlines, and submission requirements for abstracts to AMS meetings, letters to the Notices, meeting/advertising submissions, subscriptions, and member address changes. Includes publication practices and program/meeting-calendar caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: "Abstracts should be submitted on special forms which are available in many departments of mathematics and from the headquarters office of the Society. Abstracts of papers to be presented at the meeting must be received at the headquarters of the Society in Providence, Rhode Island, on or before the deadline given below for the meeting."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit using AMS special abstract forms (available from departments or AMS headquarters). Mail so abstracts are received at AMS headquarters in Providence by the stated deadline. Note that an abstract deadline may expire before publication of a first announcement; for additional information consult the meeting announcements and the list of special sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-session abstract earlier deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: "Note that the deadline for abstracts for consideration for presentation at special sessions is usually three weeks earlier than that specified below."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are submitting for a special session, plan to meet an earlier abstract deadline (typically ~3 weeks before the general abstract deadline). Check special-sessions listings and meeting announcements for exact cutoff dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts publication practice
rubrics_metrics.description: "Abstracts of papers presented at a meeting of the Society are published in the journal Abstracts of papers presented to the American Mathematical Society in the issue corresponding to that of the Notices which contains the program of the meeting, insofar as is possible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted/presented abstracts will be published in the Abstracts journal in the issue that corresponds to the Notices issue containing the program, when feasible. Timely submission is necessary to achieve corresponding publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting calendar and program caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: "This calendar lists all meetings and conferences approved prior to the date this issue went to press. The meeting dates which fall rather far in the future are subject to change; this is particularly true of meetings to which no numbers have been assigned. Programs of the meetings will appear in the issues indicated below. First and supplementary announcements of the meetings will have appeared in earlier issues."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat far-future meeting dates as tentative (especially those without assigned numbers). Expect programs to be published in specific upcoming Notices issues; consult prior issues for first/supplementary announcements. Verify dates before making plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to the Editor: review and scope policy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Letters submitted for publication in the Notices are reviewed by the Editorial Committee. The Notices does not ordinarily publish complaints about reviews of books or articles, although rebuttals and correspondence concerning reviews in Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society will be considered for publication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All letters are subject to Editorial Committee review; avoid submitting routine complaints about reviews (these are generally not published). Rebuttals specifically concerning reviews in the Bulletin may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to the Editor: format and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: "Letters should be typed and in legible form or they will be returned to the sender, possibly resulting in a delay of publication. All published letters must include the name of the author. Letters which have been, or may be, published elsewhere will be considered, but the Managing Editor of the Notices should be informed of this fact when the letter is submitted. The committee reserves the right to edit letters. Letters should be mailed to the Editor of the Notices, American Mathematical Society, P. 0. Box 6248, Providence, RI 02940, or sent by email to notices@math.ams.com, and will be acknowledged on receipt."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type letters legibly to avoid return/delay. Include the author's full name on any letter submitted for publication. Notify the Managing Editor if the letter has been or may be published elsewhere. Expect editorial changes and an acknowledgement of receipt when mailed or emailed to the provided addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and classified content acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Notices publishes situations wanted and classified advertising, and display advertising for publishers and academic or scientific organizations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifieds (e.g., job notices, situations wanted) and display ads from publishers/academic/scientific organizations are accepted. Contact the AMS Advertising Department for the Advertising Rate Card and specific display-ad deadlines and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for classifieds, news items, and meeting announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabulated deadlines are given for Classified Ads, News Items, and Meeting Announcements (e.g., sample dates: Classified Ads — October 1, 1992; News Items — September 21, 1992; Meeting Announcements — September 21, 1992 for the November issue; other dated deadlines for subsequent issues are listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the issue-specific submission deadlines listed in the Notices for the type of material you are submitting. Deadlines vary by issue; consult the Notices' deadlines table well in advance and contact Advertising or Customer Services when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription and ordering policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscription prices for Volume 39 (1992) are $131 list; $105 institutional member; $79 individual member. "A late charge of 10% of the subscription price will be imposed upon orders received from nonmembers after January 1 of the subscription year. Add for postage: Surface delivery outside the United States and India — $15; to India — $28; expedited delivery to destinations in North America — $32; elsewhere — $67. Subscriptions and orders for AMS publications should be addressed to the American Mathematical Society, P.O. Box 1571, Annex Station, Providence, RI 02901-1571. All orders must be prepaid."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepay all subscription/orders. Nonmember late orders (after Jan 1) incur a 10% late charge. Add specified postage/expedited delivery charges for international shipments. Use the listed AMS P.O. Box for subscriptions and orders and the toll-free phone number for card orders within U.S./Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of address: timing and required information
rubrics_metrics.description: "Members of the Society who move or who change positions are urged to notify the Providence Office as soon as possible. Journal mailing lists must be printed four to six weeks before the issue date. Therefore, in order to avoid disruption of service, members are requested to provide the required notice well in advance... If your address has changed or will change within the next two or three months, please fill out this form, supply any other information appropriate for the AMS records, and mail to the address given below."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide change-of-address notification well in advance (journal mailing lists printed 4–6 weeks before issue). Complete the provided form or email the requested details (name, customer code, change effective date, old/new mailing address, new position, new employer and location, telephone numbers, electronic addresses, recent honors/awards, personal items for publication) and send to Customer Services (mail or provided email addresses) to avoid service disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business-reply and form submission instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Business-reply mail and forms (e.g., Change of Address, donation pledge forms) are provided with instructions; mail completed forms to AMS Customer Services (P.O. Box 6248) or use specified email addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the business-reply envelope/forms as directed; fold/mail to the designated P.O. Box or email provided addresses (amsmem@math.ams.com or cust-serv@math.ams.com) for faster processing. Follow the form fields and checkboxes (e.g., credit card options, pledge amounts, publication printing opt-out) as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: FSU Aid Fund: matching and donation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Sloan Foundation has awarded the AMS a $30,000 challenge grant to support the AMS fSU AID FUND. Contributions to the fund will now be matched on a dollar-for-dollar basis... Enclosed is my (our) gift or pledge of: $1000, $500, $250, $100, other ____ (Pledges are encouraged to be fulfilled within the year ending 9/1/93)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donations to the AMS fSU Aid Fund are matched dollar-for-dollar up to $30,000. When giving by credit card, note the minimum gift of $20 for VISA/MasterCard. Pledges should ideally be fulfilled within the fiscal window stated. Use the donation form or contact AMS Development Office for further instructions and tax-deduction details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and acknowledgements for mailed/email submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Letters should be mailed to the Editor... or sent by email to notices@math.ams.com, and will be acknowledged on receipt."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect an acknowledgement when mailing or emailing letters/submissions to the provided addresses; retain proof of submission and include contact information to facilitate acknowledgement and follow-up.
